resources.string: Smart DNS
Use a proxying DNS provider for Iran-blocked sites (Gemini, AI tools, developer services); Aether still opens filtered sites.
Use Smart DNS
Resolves names with these servers instead of 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8. Covered sites see the provider\'s country; other traffic keeps the WARP exit.
Only for the Aether-only chain. With Psiphon or Tor in front, the exit is already abroad; this setting is ignored.
Protocol
Plain DNS
DNS over HTTPS
DNS over TLS
DNS over UDP (TCP for large answers). Works with every provider but is unencrypted.
Queries use HTTPS and resemble web traffic. Use it when the provider supports it.
Queries use TLS on port 853. Encrypted, but port 853 is easier to block.
Smart DNS servers
e.g. https://dns.example.com/dns-query
e.g. dns.example.com
IPv4 addresses, optionally with port (1.2.3.4:5353), separated by commas, spaces, or new lines. Up to 8 servers, tried in order.
HTTPS URLs or host names; path defaults to /dns-query. Up to 8 servers, tried in order.
Host names or IPv4 addresses, optionally with port (default 853). Up to 8 servers, tried in order.
No usable server for this protocol. Default DNS resolvers are used until one is valid.
Queries use the tunnel first. If the provider answers only Iranian or registered IPs, Aether reaches it directly and sends its proxies directly too.
Now: through the tunnel.
Now: direct (provider rejected the tunnel). Proxy ranges detected: %1$d.

Android\'s Private DNS (Settings, Network, Private DNS) must be Off or Automatic; otherwise Smart DNS is ignored. IPv6 is unavailable to apps while it is on. Test with a covered site, not an IP checker.
